transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you know, we've got a 48-hour water conservation restriction from the municipal water authority, and we need to reduce our normal process-water consumption during that period. I'll be making the final call on the water-control plan, but I want to hear from quality, maintenance, and EHS before I sign off. Let's start the conservation huddle. What updates do you each have?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have an important quality update. My lab test, completed this morning but not yet uploaded to the shared quality folder, found reclaimed-water conductivity at 1,800 microsiemens per centimeter. Line X's process limit is 1,200, while Line Y's process limit is 2,200. Line Y's scheduled batch requires exactly 1,800 liters, so reclaimed water is acceptable for that batch only after a conductivity test is recorded.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a maintenance update. My inspection of the recovery skid, documented in my maintenance notebook but not yet entered in the work-order system, found that the skid requires an exact 3-hour membrane flush before use and can then deliver reclaimed water at no more than 600 liters per hour.
transcript.speaker: A3

My permit review with the municipal inspector yesterday, which is awaiting attachment to the site's permit record, found that reclaimed water may be used only after its residual sanitizer is adjusted to exactly 0.3 parts per million, and that each use day requires a signed sanitizer log.

decisions.reclaimed_water_plan: Use reclaimed water for Line Y's scheduled batch only. Do not use reclaimed water for Line X due to conductivity exceeding its process limit.

commitments.detail: Ravi must upload the completed conductivity test to the shared quality folder before reclaimed water is used for Line Y's batch.
Jon must ensure the sanitizer is adjusted to exactly 0.3 ppm and a signed sanitizer log is completed for each use day.
Mei must enter the 3-hour membrane flush requirement in the work-order system and confirm the skid can deliver at 600 liters per hour before use.
